metadata.title: HDBLAST: Stationary Quantum Shell Closure with Paired de Sitter Sources
metadata.description:
This prospective computational checkpoint studies stationary shell backreaction in a declared dimensionless model with one free, minimally coupled massive shell scalar in the Euclidean/Bunch–Davies de Sitter state. An original quadratic mass interaction and a fixed-reference common action supply paired metric and scalar sources, which are updated together while solving the regular bulk and both shell junctions. The archive includes the full source Hessian, a bounded amplitude scan, integration refinements, an independent acceleration-system implementation, separate proper-time endpoint checks, negative controls, and a distinct sampled gravitational hierarchy screen.

The mathematical model fixes N=1 and gamma=kappa5²/L³ for positive gamma; gamma=0 is the disabled-source classical control. The mass law, finite matching, and gravitational normalization are declared research choices, not measurements. Large-gamma roots are formal closure stress cases and do not establish controlled effective field theory. Static numerical closure is distinct from a rigorous existence or uniqueness theorem, causal response, dynamical stability, radiation production, thermalization, or heating. Self-consistent iteration of one-loop sources does not calculate all two-loop physics.

The archive preserves prospective registration provenance, source hashes, original results and failures when present, and separately identified post-run audits. The theory includes the fixed-positive-curvature mass-zero obstruction for the quadratic interaction. Literature verification supplies context and dimensional limits without establishing novelty or priority. Separate AI-assisted derivations, implementations and review are internal cross-checks, not external peer review.

Reproduction requires the pinned inherited inputs in a full HDBLAST repository checkout; a checkpoint-only ZIP is not self-contained. Text, figures and data are licensed under CC BY 4.0.
